title.narrative: Output 7.1. Increased capacity of the member States to ensure respect for, promote and realize fundamental principles and rights at work

description.narrative: In 2020, the Federal Government adopted the National Plan on LGBTI Employment, with a focus on the transgender population. The National Plan was designed on the understanding that non-discrimination is crucial to promoting fundamental principles and rights at work (FPRW). The Plan addresses all four FPRW by: (a) promoting the inclusion of vulnerable groups in the formal labour market; (b) implementing strategies to prevent trafficking in persons (TiP) and child labour (especially sexual exploitation); and promoting tripartism, non-discrimination and collective bargaining in all of its actions. As most of the TiP victims are transgender women, one of the objectives of the National Plan is to protect transgender people from labour exploitation. As a member of the working group on the national plan on LGBTI Employment, the ILO organized four public discussions These discussions focussed on the importance of an integrated approach to FPRW, emphasizing that non-discrimination is key to preventing child labour and forced labour as well as the importance of promoting collective bargaining. The discussions highlighted related ILO Conventions and other good practices, in particular the Kitchen & Voice project experience, recognized as a good practice by the Federal Government, integrating all FPRW by promoting the inclusion of the most vulnerable groups (transgender people) into the formal labour market. Specifically, the meetings focussed on the following aspects of the project: (a) professional training for people in vulnerable situations and for victims of trafficking in persons or other forms of labour exploitation; and (b) the use of digital media for distance learning, including the professional training and new modules. The meetings highlighted how this new virtual methodology was able to reach more people, including those who live in areas far from urban centres that were previously not included in the public policies. The discussions demonstrated how the Kitchen& Voice distance methodology decreased the cost of the course, making it more accessible and viable for dissemination. Part of the national plan and its implementation strategy were based on these experiences of the Kitchen & Voice project. The ILO also engaged worker organizations and companies to be part of the discussions. The ILO continues working with the government to implement the plan and improve its initiatives.

title.narrative: 7.1.1. Number of member States with integrated programmes on fundamental principles and rights at work
Output 5.1. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to identify current skills mismatches and anticipate future skill needs

description.narrative:
Skills mismatches and future skill needs for the textile and clothing industries identified, measured, and anticipated by Brazil's federal government, employers' and workers' organizations, and tripartite recommendations discussed and approved. The process was based on the Prospective Model developed by the National Service of Industrial Training (SENAI), an institution linked to the Brazilian National Confederation of Industry (CNI).
Throughout 2020, the ILO led the establishment of the "Working group on the future of work in the textile and clothing sector", a tripartite body composed by the Brazilian Cooperation Agency (ABC), the Brazilian Textile and Apparel Industry Association (Abit), the Unified Workers' Central (CUT), the Ministry of Economy and SENAI. The working group revised the "SENAI's Prospective Study for future industrial occupations for the Brazilian Textile and Clothing Sector". A total of 138 recommendations directed to professional training institutions, federal government ministries and secretariats, sector associations, workers unions, textile companies and research institutions were formulated and approved by the working group. The recommendations are important to support the sector to face the post COVID-19 pandemic challenges. They were shared by Abit with the "Sustainable Fashion Initiative", which gather organizations of the fashion sector, and they were also included in Abit's document "Vision for the Future of Textile and Apparel Sector". Abit has also discussed the recommendations internally (such as steering committee meetings) and externally. This work was considered innovative by the Brazilian constituents with potential for sharing. The ILO, through its Cotton with Decent Work Project funded by Brazil, led and conducted an online survey with 40 specialists, organized and compiled the information of the survey which served as input to the development of the sector´s adopted recommendations. To adopt the recommendations, the ILO also conducted a series of online tripartite consultation meetings. The final document was also edited and disseminated by the ILO.

Output 5.3. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative:
The government of the municipality of Goiás adopted as a public policy an inclusive and innovative skills programme "Saberes das Mãos" for women in vulnerable situations (victims of domestic violence, over 60 years old, afro-descendants, unemployed). Initially implemented by the NGO Mulheres Coralinas Association, the programme supports the beneficiaries to develop skills, such as handicrafts, embroidery, ceramics, natural fibers, gastronomy and needlework, including the production of face masks. The local government took great interest supporting the dissemination/sales of the products, increased the number of beneficiaries and allocated a space to serve as headquarters for the project. About 150 women were reached by the programme. Most of these women are more than 60 years old and with no other means to provide for themselves. Moreover, the majority of them suffered domestic violence, and have no psychological or financial resources to change their lives.
The work is aimed not only at providing the beneficiaries with income generation opportunities and developing their personal skills, but also to create a network where women can feel protected, share their experiences and concerns, and strengthen their existing cooperative. They also use poetry as a learning process, especially from two poets born in the same town of Goiás: Cora Coralina and Leodegária de Jesus.
With the COVID-19 pandemic, training was conducted online, using innovative methodologies and tools. Materials were delivered to their homes and they were paid for their production during the training (the only source of income for most of the participants). The ILO technically supported the NGO Mulheres Coralinas Association to develop the training methodology and purchase the necessary equipment for the professional training. Additionally, the ILO held several meetings with the local government and Mulheres Coralinas Association to include this programme as a public policy.

title.narrative: 5.3.2. Number of member States with innovative, flexible and inclusive skills programmes and services targeting women, youth or persons in vulnerable situations
Output 5.3. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative:
Through the ILO concepts of quality apprenticeships and work-based learning, a pilot programme was implemented in the city of Cristalina, (State of Goiás) from January 2020. The Inclusive Professional Apprenticeship (API in Portuguese), aims at vulnerable adolescents/youth that many times could not follow the "traditional" apprenticeship programs due to social, emotional and/or educational gaps, and takes place in the real work environment.
API is based on the understanding of the Labour Prosecutor's Office – MPT, and the Ministry of Economy (both the Secretariat of Labor Inspection – SIT -cand the Secretariat of Public Policies for Employment – SPPE), that the Brazilian Apprenticeship Law has great potential for combatting/preventing child labor, in the age group of its highest incidence (80%), between 14-17 years.
API's strategy established partnerships with employers' and workers' organizations, educational entities and local governments, in order to achieve a collaborative construction of the programme, based on the development of socio-emotional and technical skills, specifically designed for the vulnerable population. The ILO led the creation of the Working Group (formed by the Ministry of Economy and the MPT) responsible for formulating the basic premises of API: - API must be tested as a pilot, allowing for the monitoring and evaluation and further expansion of the initiative at the national level. - API will develop socio-emotional and technical skills, which means that educational entities must incorporate the social technologies specifically designed for vulnerable population. - The API Program should last 2 years (maximum period allowed by law), with greater concentration of the theoretical load at the beginning of the calendar. - Companies must play an active role regarding the specific technical skills developed both in-school and in the work environment. - Local governments (Municipal Secretariats of Education and Social Assistance) must play an active role in the identification of adolescents/youth with API's profile. - API will not depend in any legislative alterations. On the contrary, it will seek to optimize the current legislation, structure, and financing arrangements.
The ILO Led the expansion of the Working Group, including educational entities of the State of Goiás, as well as employers' and workers' organizations, and the municipality of Cristalina, allowing for the development of two learning modules and the conformation of the first class of the API Program in the Commerce and Service Sector, with 22 apprentices hired by 13 local companies.
